findings.title: id=27 — Unauthenticated raw server errors are neither graceful nor consistently handled (raw Sequelize WHERE errors and TypeError stack traces exposed)
findings.analysis: The application exposes unauthenticated raw server errors without graceful wrapping and renders them inconsistently by content type. Primary trigger (GET /rest/user/security-question with no parameters) returns HTTP 500 with a raw Sequelize WHERE error ('WHERE parameter "email" has invalid "undefined" value') plus a full stack trace including internal file paths (/juice-shop/node_modules/sequelize/lib/dialects/abstract/query-generator.js, /juice-shop/node_modules/sequelize/lib/model.js:1140:47) and a stack frame identifying the unauthenticatable SecurityAnswer model — 500/2946 B text/html, sha256 0b84d83c08cc28421da7b67c32d997676e490f8bd4016854f849200c2e11a90b. The identical request with Accept: application/json returns HTTP 500 with the same error rendered as a raw JSON error object with its own stack trace — 500/1804 B application/json, sha256 20eec46aa7555e7df9a45e29f3ef1a525bfc60e64645def1e662c629c0419b9e. The single-header change (Accept) alters error-body shape, proving the errors are not consistently handled. Corroborating independent trigger (GET /redirect?continue=) returns HTTP 500 TypeError 'Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'includes')' with a full stack through /juice-shop/build/lib/insecurity.js and /juice-shop/build/routes/redirect.js — 500/2531 B, sha256 020023ff4f9ae2b934531ecd4f7f04d012a055a23b67e99de52dbc3f7ec4ec48. Null/control comparison (GET /api/Nonexistent/1) returns HTTP 500 'Unexpected path' without a stack trace — 500/2436 B, sha256 5b9004f21283f4ac5240d03066c6cd5d19aa7891c8f2d30011651dbbb01f3718 — demonstrating that graceful handling exists elsewhere in the application for other routes, so the raw-stack exposure is a real inconsistency rather than the app-wide norm. Severity rationale: unauthenticated exposure of raw SQL query logic, internal module paths, and stack frames aids reconnaissance and is a security misconfiguration regardless of direct exploitability.
findings.false_positive_check: The behavior is not benign for three independent reasons. (1) It is raw-stack, not a generic framework 500: the body contains an unredacted Sequelize WHERE diagnostic, internal sequelize module paths and line numbers, and an unauthenticatable model reference (SecurityAnswer.findAll) — a benign app-wide 500 page would contain neither. (2) The Accept: application/json variant renders the identical request as a different raw-body shape (2946 B HTML raw error vs 1804 B JSON raw error), so the claim is not an artifact of one client; the error handling is representation-dependent and therefore inconsistent. (3) The null control (GET /api/Nonexistent/1) shows the application IS capable of graceful 500 handling without a stack ('Unexpected path' wrapper), so the raw errors on the viable routes are a localized inconsistency, not an unavoidable server default. The independent /redirect TypeError trigger reproduces the class with a completely different code path and error type, ruling out a single-route anomaly.

findings.title: id=97 — Unauthenticated Prometheus-style metrics endpoint exposes application usage telemetry (LLM usage counters, request counts, solved-challenge counters)
findings.analysis: The /metrics endpoint is served to any unauthenticated requester as Prometheus-format text (HTTP 200, text/plain; version=0.0.4) serving 26181 B of application telemetry. Body contains juiceshop_llm_input_tokens_total / juiceshop_llm_input_tokens / juiceshop_llm_output_tokens_total / juiceshop_llm_output_tokens / juiceshop_llm_tool_calls_total counters (app='juiceshop'), http_requests_count grouped by status code (2XX/3XX/4XX/5XX), file_uploads_count, file_upload_errors, juiceshop_version_info=20.2.0, and juiceshop_challenges_solved labels (difficulty and category buckets), plus standard process_* gauges. The endpoint is unauthenticated: an invalid Bearer token is ignored and the same 200 body is returned with no Set-Cookie header. Secrets scan of the body is clean (no tokens, keys, or credentials embedded in the metrics stream). This is the exposed-metrics behavior: an unauthenticated operational endpoint leaking application usage telemetry and challenge-solved classification, available to anyone who can reach the worker endpoint.
findings.false_positive_check: The behavior is not a benign health probe. (1) Content-type and body shape are Prometheus text-format (HELP/TYPE lines, counter/gauge metrics), not a thin health check — it carries application-level usage counters, not merely up/alive status. (2) It is served unauthenticated (invalid Bearer -> 200, no auth check), so it is not a protected dashboard requiring login; the telemetry is globally readable. (3) It includes juiceshop_challenges_solved labels by difficulty and category, which disclose which challenge classes the application tracks/has solved — a classification leak beyond raw health data. The response is stable (200/26181 B, sha256 060c408bf7881b5ebd6364cde3f3d46c988eaf5c9fba963c0efefd7a552c3ed0) and the claim anchors on gauge presence and Prometheus format rather than volatile byte counts, so the claim survives normal counter drift.
